live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust-built ransomware-as-a-service that hit hospitals, cities and casinos before going dark
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, sold ransomware to affiliates from late 2021. Reports tie it to dozens of high-profile victims. Its infrastructure was disrupted in December 2023, and it appeared to exit scam in March 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also known as ALPHVM, BlackCat, BlackCat Gang, Noberus, Ambitious Scorpius and UNC4466.
It runs as ransomware-as-a-service. The core team sells the malware as a subscription, and affiliates carry out the attacks.
According to Malpedia, the ransomware is written in Rust and runs on Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi. Malpedia says it has been seen in attacks since 18 November 2021.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter operations.
S2W found that some BlackCat configuration fields match BlackMatter's. It still found it difficult to conclude they are the same group.
Cisco Talos calls the links between the BlackMatter/DarkSide ring and BlackCat probable. It has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were among BlackCat's early adopters.
Talos also notes that a BlackCat representative told Recorded Future the two groups were connected, but that BlackCat was not a rebranding of BlackMatter.
Mandiant tracks the ALPHV operator as UNC3507.
BleepingComputer reports that the FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months, from November 2021 to March 2022.
The same report says the FBI estimates the gang took at least $300 million in ransom from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.

Victims named in the reports include a US city, Alexandria in Louisiana, and Suffolk County in New York. DataBreaches reports that BlackCat claimed the Suffolk attack, which disabled the county's 911 system.

Recorded Future News says the group has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical companies. It reported that the gang listed India's largest drugmaker, Sun Pharmaceuticals, on its leak site.

Other victims were a dental and medical distributor, Henry Schein, a Canadian software group, Constellation Software, and a French IT firm, Inetum. For Inetum, the BlackCat attribution came from an editor at LeMagIt, not the company.
In a 2023 case Sygnia investigated, access came through a compromised third-party vendor. Sygnia attributes that attack to BlackCat or one of its affiliates.
In that case the attacker moved sideways over several weeks with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools. It copied data out with Rclone and then sent extortion emails.
eSentire reports that Russian-speaking affiliates used Google ads to lure users to sites that delivered Nitrogen, an initial-access malware that led to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware.
Malpedia says the ransomware can encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20, delete volume shadow copies and stop ESXi virtual machines. It can also spread to other hosts using PsExec.
Symantec describes 2022 updates that added an ARM build, safe-mode encryption and searchable leak data. It also saw an affiliate use the Eamfo infostealer against Veeam backup credentials.
Talos says BlackCat is used in double-extortion attacks, where data is stolen as well as encrypted.
ReliaQuest reports that Scattered Spider gains access through partnerships with ransomware operators, including ALPHV.
The catalogue lists tools tied to the group, including Mimikatz, PsExec, Impacket, LaZagne and MEGAsync.
In a statement relayed by the press, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors at MGM Resorts on 11 September 2023. These are the group's own unverified claims.
BleepingComputer reports that an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites in December 2023. It describes the takedown as temporary.
In February 2024, BleepingComputer reported that unnamed sources linked the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. It could not confirm this, and BlackCat had not claimed the attack at the time.
The US State Department offered rewards of up to $10 million for information on the group's leadership, and $5 million for people linked to its attacks.
In March 2024 BleepingComputer concluded the gang was running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and it offered its source code for $5 million.
The gang also posted a fake FBI seizure banner. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved, and ALPHV told the report its infrastructure had been seized.
Malpedia lists a US Justice Department release dated 30 December 2025. It says two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Treat a leak-site claim as a claim until the victim or investigators confirm it.
Backups, vendor access and remote-management tools are worth checking first, since the reports above describe attackers going after all three.
